**Finding: COMPLIANT (preferred position) — no redline proposed.**

**What I checked:**
- Full-document searches for "minimum", take-or-pay, shortfall, commit to purchase, volume/quantity/forecast, requirements/sole-source, and "payable whether or not used" — all negative except insurance limits (Sections 11.6–11.6.1, p0573–p0577), which are irrelevant to this rule.
- Article 6 (Payments and Records): AbbVie's obligations are a one-time upfront payment (§6.1, $30M), milestone payments contingent on achievement of specified development/regulatory events (§6.2), and royalties on actual Net Sales. Nothing is payable for unpurchased volume.
- Article 4 (Commercialization): §4.5.1 gives AbbVie the **sole right** to Manufacture and supply Licensed Compounds/Products at its own expense, and §4.5.2 gives AbbVie a manufacturing technology transfer right — the opposite of a requirements or sourcing obligation to Harpoon.

**Why preferred, not fallback:** There is no minimum purchase or volume commitment on AbbVie at all, and AbbVie pays only on the occurrence of ordered/achieved events and actual sales. Both preferred elements are satisfied by the bargain as drafted, so the fallback machinery (12-month scope, 30-day reduction notice, true-up) is unnecessary — there is no commitment to limit, reduce, or true up. Inserting an affirmative "no minimum commitment" recital would be non-operative boilerplate in a development-and-option structure with no purchase mechanic.

**Noted, not flagged:** §4.2's Commercially Reasonable Efforts commercialization diligence obligation binds AbbVie, but it is an efforts standard rather than a volume or purchase commitment; it belongs to a separate commercial rule and is deliberately not double-flagged here.
